content.document_title: Recommendations for Diagnosis of Pulmonary Embolism (PE)
content.summary: Guidance on diagnostic approach to suspected PE, including use of clinical probability assessment, D-dimer testing, imaging (CTPA, V/Q scintigraphy/SPECT), lower-limb compression ultrasonography (CUS) and MRA.

sections.recommendation: In suspected high-risk PE with haemodynamic instability, perform bedside echocardiography or emergency CTPA if available. Initiate IV anticoagulation with unfractionated heparin (weight-adjusted bolus) without delay in patients with suspected high-risk PE.

Use validated criteria to estimate probability of PE. Initiation of anticoagulation is recommended without delay in patients with high or intermediate clinical probability while diagnostic workup is in progress.
Diagnostic strategy should be based on clinical probability assessed by clinical judgement or a validated prediction rule.

Measure plasma D-dimer using a highly sensitive assay in outpatients/emergency-department patients with low or intermediate clinical probability (or those PE-unlikely) to reduce unnecessary imaging. Consider an age-adjusted D-dimer cut-off as an alternative to a fixed cut-off (age × 10 µg/L for patients >50 years). D-dimer is not recommended to exclude PE in patients with high clinical probability.
sections.class_level: Recommendations range: Class I Level A (sensitive D-dimer use); Class IIa Level B (age-adjusted); Class III Level A (not for high-probability)

sections.recommendation: If CTPA is normal in a patient with low or intermediate clinical probability, reject the diagnosis of PE. Accept diagnosis of PE if CTPA shows a segmental or more proximal filling defect in a patient with intermediate or high clinical probability. In patients with high clinical probability and a normal CTPA, consider further testing or additional imaging.
sections.class_level: Class I–IIa, Levels A–B depending on scenario

sections.recommendation: Reject the diagnosis of PE (without further testing) if perfusion scan is normal. Consider accepting diagnosis (without further testing) if V/Q scan yields high probability. A non-diagnostic V/Q scan combined with a negative proximal CUS can be considered to exclude PE in patients with low clinical probability or those PE-unlikely.
V/Q SPECT may be considered for PE diagnosis in centers where available.

Accept diagnosis of VTE (and support PE diagnosis) if CUS shows a proximal DVT in a patient with clinical suspicion of PE. If CUS shows only a distal DVT, further testing (imaging) should be considered to confirm PE. If a positive proximal CUS is used to confirm PE, assessment of PE severity should be considered to permit risk-adjusted management.
sections.class_level: Class I–IIa, Levels A–B (severity assessment Level C)

sections.recommendation: MRA is not recommended for ruling out PE.

sections.content: CT = computed tomographic; CTPA = computed tomography pulmonary angiography; CUS = compression ultrasonography; DVT = deep vein thrombosis; i.v. = intravenous; MRA = magnetic resonance angiography; PE = pulmonary embolism; SPECT = single-photon emission computed tomography; UFH = unfractionated heparin; V/Q = ventilation/perfusion; VTE = venous thromboembolism.
